To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of a ground-shielded corona electrode increases both the corona current intensity and the charge acquired by insulating particles placed on the grounded plate electrode.
the grounded shield increases the current intensity of the corona, decreases the inception voltage of corona, and increases the charge acquired by particles deposited at the grounded plate.

a grounded metal shield placed in the proximity of the wire electrode facing the grounded plate increases the current intensity and decreases the inception voltage of corona discharge generated at the wire, both in the presence and in the absence of a layer of dielectric particles at the surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the optimization of the wire-plate electrode arrangement in order to increase the corona discharge efficiency for the charging of nonwoven fabrics, granular insulating materials, and other applications.
the optimization of a corona charging electrode arrangement, with the aim of improving the efficiency of the corona charging process in electrostatic separators.
the development of a new electrode arrangement, with a ground-shielded high-voltage electrode facing a grounded electrode, for corona discharge applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of a metallic shield in the vicinity of the corona wire electrode increases the charge transfer efficiency of a wire-plate configuration, both in the presence and in the absence of insulating particles.
the grounded shield improves the performance of the corona charging system by reducing the inception voltage, increasing the current intensity, and increasing the charging rate of the particles.
the presence of the grounded metallic shield improves the performance of the wire-plate electrode arrangement for electrostatic charging applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of a shielded electrode in corona charging applications can increase the current density and the charging efficiency of the collecting electrode.

the grounded shield increases the corona discharge current and the charge deposited on a grounded plate electrode, and the effect is more pronounced for higher applied voltages and larger shield distances.

the presence of a metallic shield in the vicinity of a corona wire electrode facing a grounded plane electrode increases the current intensity, decreases the inception voltage, increases the charge density, and increases the charge acquisition efficiency of the grounded electrode.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the grounded metallic shield is able to increase the corona charging efficiency of the wire-plate electrode arrangement.
the presence of a metallic shield in the vicinity of a wire electrode facing a grounded plane can be beneficial for corona charging applications.
a grounded metallic shield can be used to increase the corona current and charge deposited by a wire electrode, which is a useful feature for electrostatic applications.
